# Writing frontmatter, one page per doctype

<!-- GENERATED by taxidermist from taxonomy/. Do not hand-edit: edit the schema and run `taxidermist docs`. -->

Each page resolves one `type:`: its obligations, a fill-in template, what to put in every field and every vocabulary it uses. Generated from [..](../README.md), which is the schema and the thing to edit.

- [`Project Plan`](project-plan.md)
- [`meeting`](meeting.md)
- [`note`](note.md)
- [`person`](person.md)

## Folders

A folder name directly under these directories, or the filename of a page sitting directly there, must be an allowed value. `index.md` and `README.md` there describe the directory itself.

- `projects/<name>`: `<name>` is a value of [`topic`](../vocabularies/topic.yaml). A file whose `topic:` names a different value gets a warning.
- `people/<name>`: `<name>` matches `^[a-z][a-z-]*$`.

## What holds on every page

**Frontmatter describes the document.** The body carries the content; frontmatter is
what a query filters on.

**A field's `definitions` keys are its allowed values.** There is no second list, so a value cannot exist until someone writes down what it means. Prefer an existing one, because a near-synonym fragments every filter. If nothing fits, add it to the right file under [..](../README.md) with its one line in the same change, then run `taxidermist docs`. `taxidermist check` blocks the commit otherwise.

**YAML frontmatter is hand-written and fails silently.** A block that opens and does not parse leaves the file invisible to every tool that reads it, while it looks correct on disk. An unescaped quote, or a `: ` inside an unquoted scalar, is where it usually breaks.
